Sosyal güvenlik katkıları: The portion of labor income paid to the social security institutions.
Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumları Bütçesi: The budget of the public administrations providing social security services, such as the Social Security Institution and the Turkish Employment Agency.
Sosyal Sermaye: The concept expressing the values in social life of the bonds, union, togetherness, solidarity, mutual assistance, love, respect, trust and morality among individuals.
Special and Exclusive Rights: Special rights are the rights given by the state, through any legal, regulatory or administrative way, to a limited number of undertakings, to be within a certain geographical area. An exclusive right, on the other hand, is the right arising from the state's establishing a monopoly, through any legal instrument, in favor of a single undertaking (public or private) for the conduct of a certain economic activity in a certain geographical area for a certain period.
Spekülasyon güdüsü: The demand for money stemming from the thought of making gains from the expected future price changes of financial or non-financial assets.
Spot Piyasa: The market in which the purchase or sale of a product is realized, at the price determined on the transaction date, at the latest within two business days thereafter.
Spot Valör: The realization, within two business days following the day on which the transaction is made, of the payments connected with a transaction carried out in the financial markets. If a transaction made with spot value date, for example, took place on Monday, the payments are made on Wednesday. In other words, the spot value date expresses the date on which the money will be ready for use. The difference between the transaction date and the date of use stems from operations such as the preparation of messages, the making of controls and the provision of funds requiring a certain time.
Stackelberg modeli: A duopoly model in which one of the two identical firms producing a homogeneous product makes its output choice being aware of the mutual interdependence, while the other is unaware of it.
Stagflasyon: Refers to the situation that occurs when inflation rises in an environment in which production in an economy has fallen or at least has not increased.
Standart sapma: The square-rooted measure of the deviation of the returns from their average; it is the standard gauge of total risk (volatility) in finance.
Standart Vadeli İşlemler: It means forward transactions. It envisages the delivery of a certain instrument, at a previously determined price, again on a previously determined date. Its difference from forward markets is that it trades over contracts standardized in organized markets (such as the quantity of a contract, the market release dates of the contracts, and having a collateral system under the name of margin). When done for speculative purposes, theoretically there is the possibility of infinite profit and loss.
Standart Vadeli İşlemler Sözleşmesi: The contract giving the parties to the contract the obligation to buy or sell, at the agreed price, a good or instrument of standardized quality and quantity, on a determined future date.
Start-Up Costs: The establishment costs incurred for the building, vehicles, machinery, equipment, legal expenses, advertising, worker training, etc. necessary to begin an activity. Particularly in cases where these costs carry the nature of sunk costs, entry into the market becomes significantly more difficult.
Statute of Limitations: The periods regulated in Articles 20 and 21 of the Misdemeanors Law No. 5326, which prevent the Competition Board from deciding on an administrative fine (the limitation of the investigation) or the implementation of this decision (the limitation of implementation).
Sterilizasyon: The open market operations central banks make in order to balance the effects of the increases in the money supply arising for various reasons. For example, when the central bank buys foreign currency, it tries to withdraw the increase in the money supply from the market through the sale of securities, thereby sterilizing the intervention made in the foreign exchange market.
Stok: The ready productions awaiting sale in order to generate income in the future.
Strategic Behaviour: Acting strategically, taking into account also the behaviors of the other persons who can affect the decision. Instead of the assumption in classical economics that each person will take their decisions independently of the others' reactions, it is thought within the framework of game theory that persons will decide taking also the others' reactions into account.
Strategic Cooperation: (Strategic Alliance) The contract-based agreements made by two or more undertakings, preserving their own autonomy, with the aim of jointly carrying out the specific activities — such as technology, expertise, production — in which they have a competitive advantage relative to one another, or of reaching common goals; they lie between simple commercial contracts and merger transactions, are short-term, flexibly structured, and require no establishment of a new legal entity (no change of control)
Strateji: The term for the choices economic units make in order to reach their aims.
Stratejik Yatırım: The investments of strategic importance, having the potential to raise our international competitiveness, directed toward the production of products with high import dependence, with the aim of reducing the current account deficit.
Stratejik Ürün: The term for the intermediate goods with a high import ratio, whose domestic production is encouraged through various support mechanisms, with the aim of reducing the current account deficit.
Structure - ConductPerformance Paradigm: According to this approach, developed in the 1940s and playing a determining role in the American industrial economics literature between 1940 and 1970, an industry's performance depends, depending on the structure of the market, on the behaviors of the buyers and sellers in the market; the market structure in turn depends on fundamental conditions such as technology and demand. Hence structure is used as the predictor of conduct and performance. The market's structure (such as full competition, monopoly, monopolistic competition, oligopoly) is generally defined with concentration rates
Subprime Piyasalar: The markets where persons with a poor credit history can obtain credit at a higher interest. If this credit has been taken for the purpose of buying a home, it is called 'subprime mortgage'. The institutions extending the credit can re-release these credits to the market by dividing them into risk groups and can seek investors who will purchase them.
Subsidiary: The concept of an affiliated company refers to the company of which an undertaking has, directly or indirectly, more than half of its capital or its commercial assets, the authority to exercise more than half of the voting rights, the authority to appoint more than half of the members of the audit board, the board of directors or the organs legally authorized to represent the business, or the right to manage its business.
Substitutability: Substitutability refers to the ability of goods or services to be used in place of another good or service in production or consumption. Substitutability results in producers/consumers moving between the two products when the demands of the two products interact with one another and it is profitable. Substitute goods have a positive cross-price elasticity of demand. From the standpoint of competition law, whether the two products take place in the same market is determined according to the degree of substitution between the products
Sukuk: The Islamic financing certificate issued for asset financing, based on the principle that the income to be obtained from the asset or investment purchased with the fund obtained through its issuance is paid to the sukuk holders at certain periods. In its simplest form, sukuk shows the ownership of an asset or the right to benefit from it. The right and claim contained in the sukuk is not only the right to a cash flow, but also the right of ownership. This differentiates the sukuk from conventional bonds. While conventional bonds consist of interest-bearing securities, the sukuk is fundamentally a security consisting of the right of ownership in an asset basket. The bond can be characterized as a debt-based certificate, and the sukuk as an asset-based certificate.
Super Dominance: The concept of super-dominance is used to express the market power approaching monopoly, as a result of the market power's persisting for a long time. It corresponds to the power held by monopolies or near-monopoly undertakings, and approximately over 90% market share is associated with this concept.
Sweezy modeli: Or the kinked demand curve model: the oligopoly model in which the demand for a firm's good depends on the response of the rival firms to a price change.
Switching Cost: Every kind of cost the customer encounters, outside the price of the good or service, at the stage of switching to a new provider. For example, in cases where number portability among operators is not possible, the customer's changing their GSM operator creates the cost of informing the persons in the phone book about the number change. The transaction cost of changing provider, the capacity to learn to use the new product, the necessity of the new product being compatible with the existing equipment, the untried brands
SWOT Analizi: An analysis method, carried out concerning the current situation, based on the determination of the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats. It is formed from the initial letters of the English words strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats. Completion Visa: the approval given that an investment made by obtaining an Investment Incentive Certificate has been completed.
Sözleşmesi: The contract arranged between the investor and the OSB relating to the allocation of the parcel, following the delivery by the real or legal persons found suitable for parcel allocation in the Organized Industrial Zones of the Investment Commitment, notarized, to the OSB.
Sübvansiyon: The unconditional payment or tax reduction made by the state, taking the public interest into account.
Sürdürülebilir büyüme: The long-run economic growth that can realistically be achieved within the framework of an action plan taking into account the limited natural resources and the environmental effects.
Sürdürülebilirlik: The method of being able to meet today's economic and social needs without restricting the possibilities of future generations and without harming nature.
Sürekli gelir: In contrast to the income obtained in the current period, the expectation of the average income that economic units think they will earn over their lifetime.
Sürekli Gelir Önsavı: The view maintaining that economic units determine their consumption not according to their income in the current period, but according to the average income they expect to earn over their lifetime.
Sürtünmesel işsizlik: Or voluntary unemployment: the type of unemployment stemming from individuals' entering and leaving the labor market and their temporary waits between jobs.
Sürü davranışı: Transacting by following the direction of the crowd instead of the individual decision; it feeds the inflation of bubbles and their collapse in panic.
Sürünen kur: The fixed exchange rate regime in which the nominal exchange rates are regularly adjusted according to selected economic indicators.
Sıfır toplamlı oyun: The situation in which the gain a participant obtains is balanced by a loss of the same magnitude belonging to the other participants.
Sıhhi Müessese: The workplace type that does not harm the environment with effects such as noise, odor and hazardous waste, by its nature. For this reason, it does not need to be located outside the settlement areas.
Sınai Mülkiyet: An intangible right ensuring that the inventions, innovations, new designs and original works in industry and agriculture are registered in the name of their first implementers, and that in the field of commerce the signs on the goods produced and sold, which will enable the distinction of their producer or seller, are registered in the name of their owners, and thereby that the first implementers have the right to produce and sell the product for a certain period.
Sınıflandırması: A classification aiming at the collection of regional statistics, their development, the making of the regions' socio-economic analyses, the determination of the framework of regional policies, and the creation of a comparable statistical database compatible with the European Union Regional Statistics System. In our country, according to this classification, 12 regions have been determined as 'Level 1', 26 sub-regions as 'Level 2', and 81 provinces as 'Level 3'.
Taban aşındırma maliyeti: The opportunity cost of the time and effort spent with the aim of avoiding the effects of inflation.
Taban fiyat: The lowest sale price determined by the state for a good or service.
Taban yıl: The year taken as the basis in calculations covering more than one year.
Takas: The transactions of the transfer of the transfer orders sent to a payment or securities settlement system, the intermediation of the mutual transmission of these orders and, in cases where pre-settlement provision is obtained, of obtaining the provision, and in some cases the netting of these orders.
Takas fiyatı: Or the market-clearing price: the price at which transactions take place when the market is in equilibrium.
Takasbank: The central clearing institution authorized to conclude the cash and securities clearing of the transactions relating to the shares, debt instruments, foreign capital market instruments, derivatives and precious metals realized in the existing markets within Borsa Istanbul. The securities delivery and receipt commitments of the Borsa Istanbul members arising from their purchase and sale transactions, and the payment commitments against the securities subject to purchase and sale, are concluded through Takasbank on an account basis. The Takasbank Electronic Transfer System (TETS) offers intermediary institutions access to the national payment system (EFT-EMKT). As the 'National Numbering Institution', Takasbank assigns ISINs (International Securities Identification Numbers), identification numbers to international standards, to the securities issued in Türkiye.
Talebin fiyat esnekliği: Or price elasticity, in short εP: a basic type of elasticity showing by what percentage the quantity demanded of a product decreases as a result of a one percent increase in its price.
